summary: Preserve Woot's browser GraphQL catalog shape, read-only boundary, gap-tolerant duplicate-aware pagination, item pricing, safely delivered output, bounded MCP access, and a verified resumable local deal archive.
reason: Woot's All Deals frontend is the authoritative searchable surface, but its mutable GraphQL paging can contain short or empty gaps and returns prices at item level. A reprint must reject GraphQL error envelopes, retain read-only CLI and MCP access, serialize catalog writers, and require two identical complete scans before destructive reconciliation.
validated_outcome: Unit tests cover paged live search, duplicate and missing-ID scan metadata, malformed GraphQL responses, atomic sync checkpoints, interprocess sync locking, mutable-snapshot verification, exact post-prune counts, no-prune incompleteness, prices, read-only provenance, GraphQL guards, MCP argument parity, and dry-run state preservation; live proof confirms priced discovery plus safe incomplete-snapshot handling when Woot's reported total exceeds its unique returned IDs.
